checks: Verified both frozen candidate hashes and the original approval hashes. Exact decoded-field comparison confirms only the statement changed, and one literal spacing replacement accounts for the entire change.

Both TeX commands insert space after the colon of the E_q set builder. The nonnegative coefficient domain, its sum-one and anchored barycenter equalities, the omitted q index, and the full quantifier scope are identical.

The strict compact-containment assumption, common κ margin, 2η perturbation estimate, exact lifted-hull fiber conclusion, proof, source locator, and dependency list are identical to the independently approved version.

Each nonempty E_q is a compact polytope inside a finite simplex. The extreme rows across all q form a finite list. Each compactly contained Minkowski sum has positive distance to the complement of the interior of K_q, so one positive ball margin works across the list. For no rows, including n=0, the margin is arbitrary.

Support of the weighted Minkowski sum is linear in the row and the added ball contributes κ on unit normals. The bound extends to every row. The perturbed inputs contribute at most η in total because their coefficients sum to one, and the perturbed target contributes at most another η. Thus κ−2η>0 and all anchored inclusions still hold.

Grouping the original lifted combination by base and deleting its q coefficient leaves either a point already in K′_q or an anchored row after renormalization. Taking the convex combination with the q contribution then gives membership in K′_q. If E_q is empty, no nontrivial such combination exists.

Each generating fiber gives the reverse inclusion and all bodies are nonempty. The projection is conv(P), whose integer points are exactly P. Taking the unperturbed family in the same argument establishes actuality.
